name: Prompt Input Card
summary: A clean, rounded prompt box sits on a calm background while a request types into it with a caret, often followed by a press on the send button. It shows the viewer how simply they ask the product for something, usually as the hook or the start of a demo.
when_to_use: Opening an AI feature by showing the question a user would ask.
Starting a demo beat where the request leads into the product's answer.
Showing a menu of presets or modes attached to an input field.

slots.name: greeting
slots.what: an optional short line above the input that sets the tone

slots.name: prompt_text
slots.what: the request the user types, one sentence in plain language

slots.name: input_chrome
slots.what: the prompt box itself with its send button and small controls

slots.name: context_ui
slots.what: simplified surrounding interface such as suggestion chips or a short list

slots.name: preset_menu
slots.what: an optional popover of modes or presets with a moving highlight

slots.name: handoff_element
slots.what: what the sent prompt turns into, such as a chat bubble or a thinking label

steps: The background and an optional greeting fade up on their own.
The prompt box and any surrounding interface assemble beneath it with a gentle stagger.
The camera pushes in so the input fills more of the frame.
The request types on character by character with a blinking caret.
A cursor moves to the send button and presses it, or a preset highlight moves to the chosen option.
The interface clears and the prompt hands off to the next scene as a bubble or a thinking state.

build.gsap: One timeline per scene. Stagger the interface pieces in with opacity and a small upward move on an expo or sine ease-out. Tween the camera wrapper's scale toward the prompt box on a slow sine in-out. Type the prompt with a stepped tween over a text counter plus a blinking caret, then tween the cursor to the send button and play a quick scale-down press. End with a fade of the surrounding interface and a scale of the prompt into its handoff element.
build.remotion: One Sequence for the assembly, one for the push-in and typing, one for the send and handoff. Drive the push-in with a heavily damped spring, slice the prompt string by an interpolated character count for the typing, and use a stiff, short spring for the button press and popover entrance.

sound: Music usually carries the scene. When there are cues, a reversed swoosh tends to land early as the box arrives, and a soft click marks the send press shortly after; an impact or glitch occasionally punctuates the handoff. Many cues are unclassified, so treat sound as optional.
caveats: Most member shots have no counted motion event, so motion timing here is thin and first motion is measured on few shots.
The most common pattern label is other; the typing itself has no measured pattern in this set.
Sound cues are sparse and many are unclassified.
